news.title: Over 270 Agartala slum residents get flats under affordable housing scheme
news.para: The Agartala Light House Project has delivered flat allotments to 278 lower-income families after an eight-year wait. This transformative initiative focuses on providing affordable housing in accordance with the GHTC-India scheme. The project features approximately 1,000 modern flats, constructed using innovative technologies for improved durability and efficiency, while also incorporating essential amenities like healthcare and community centers.

news.title: Odisha REAT upholds ₹90 lakh penalty on Puri developer, sets aside demolition
news.para: Odisha Real Estate Appellate Tribunal confirmed a Rs 90 lakh penalty for a developer violating construction plans. The developer built a G+10 structure instead of the approved G+7 residential project at Sipasarubali. The tribunal noted that mandatory approvals were not obtained for the revised plan submitted. However, it ruled that the demolition order issued by Orera exceeded jurisdiction.

news.title: LIC Housing Finance’s net profit rises 12% to ₹1,506.59 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: In Q2 FY27, LIC Housing Finance showcased a notable financial performance, with a net consolidated profit after tax of ₹1,506.59 crore, reflecting an 11.7 percent increase. Their total disbursements climbed to ₹18,127 crore, marking an 11 percent rise compared to last year. Additionally, the gross non-performing assets improved to 2.05 percent, down from 2.51 percent, and the first half's profit rose by 10.6 percent to ₹3,005.

news.title: Delhi gears up for pollution curbs from November 1; construction ban among measures
news.para: Beginning November 1, Delhi is set to introduce crucial air pollution reduction measures. These initiatives will impose limitations on older vehicle models and prohibit construction activities that create dust. To further deter private car use, parking charges will rise, while both government and private offices will embrace staggered hours and remote work policies. Authorities will take action against open burning of waste and enforce penalties for offenders.

news.title: Tamil Nadu sand truck owners announce three-day strike from November 1
news.para: From November 1 to 3, sand truck owners in Tamil Nadu are set to go on strike. This decision is rooted in their outcry against corruption within both transport and mining sectors. The Tamil Nadu State Sand Lorry Owners’ Federation is advocating for a unified e-way bill system to deter illegal operations and insists on the installation of GPS tracking devices in mineral transport.

news.title: Supertech homebuyers move SC as 17 stalled projects remain stuck, ₹30 crore spent
news.para: Homebuyers of Supertech Limited have raised significant concerns regarding the lack of progress on stalled housing projects. The Homebuyers’ Association alleges that funding for the projects has been repeatedly declined, despite available proposals. The Association urges the Supreme Court to appoint a One-Man Committee for project completion. They emphasize the financial burden on homebuyers due to growing expenses without any delivered units.

news.title: Telangana RERA bars sale of nine flats in Tellapur project after double-sale allegations
news.para: The Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has intervened in a situation involving a Sangareddy district developer facing allegations of double selling residential flats. Victims of the alleged fraud reported that they had paid significant amounts but encountered delays and unexpected requests for more funds. To safeguard the properties from further transactions that could escalate legal conflicts, the authority has issued an interim order.

news.title: IBBI tightens real estate insolvency rules to prioritise home delivery
news.para: India's insolvency regulator has implemented new rules to prioritize project completion and better homebuyer oversight. Independent assessments of construction progress and funding needs are now mandatory for real estate projects. Creditors with at least 66% voting share can recommend excluding projects from insolvency proceedings. Homebuyers will now have representation on monitoring committees to oversee implementation. These measures aim to improve transparency and protect the interests of homebuyers during insolvency.

news.title: PAG to buy 51% stake in Evergrande Property Services for $514 million
news.para: PAG is poised to acquire a controlling 51% stake in Evergrande Property Services Group for HK$4.03 billion, marking a notable transaction at a significantly discounted share price. After the trading resumption, PAG's subsidiary will be mandated to pursue the purchase of the remaining shares. This strategic move is intended to aid Evergrande's liquidators in recovering funds owed to its creditors amidst the company's ongoing financial turmoil.

news.title: Himachal Pradesh gets record bid for Wildflower Hall hotel operations
news.para: Himachal Pradesh has finalized an e-auction for the eminent Wildflower Hall Hotel, achieving a remarkable bid. The designated operator will provide 47.1 percent of the annual gross earnings, potentially yielding about Rs 2,000 crore over a span of 35 years. After a protracted legal battle lasting 25 years, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu celebrated this achievement as a critical boost to the state's finances.

news.title: Court rejects CBI's plea seeking amendment of charges against DHFL's ex-CMD, others
news.para: A Delhi court has refused to alter charges against key players in a bank fraud case, pointing to inadequate evidence from the Central Bureau of Investigation as a prime reason. Previously, the court had established certain charges against numerous accused yet discharged five others. Special Judge Sanjeev Kumar Malhotra remarked on the court's constrained ability to revisit its orders, reinforcing the sanctity of legal processes.

news.title: Delhi government extends cut off date for registration of properties in unauthorised colonies
news.para: The Delhi government has announced a new deadline for residents to secure ownership rights in unauthorized colonies, moving the date to January 31 from the original October 31. This decision comes in response to the unexpectedly low application rate. Concerns over taxes and responsibilities related to ownership are prevalent among residents. Under the PM-UDAY scheme, legal rights will be extended to individuals living in 1,511 unauthorized colonies.

news.title: JK Lakshmi Cement to invest ₹11,000 crore in 2.5 MTPA Assam plant
news.para: JK Lakshmi Cement has initiated the construction of an integrated cement plant in Umrangso, Assam, with a significant investment. This project, named Kamakshi, is expected to have a production capacity of 2.5 million tonnes per annum. The cement plant will feature a one million tonne clinkerisation unit and create over 2,000 jobs upon becoming operational. The company aims to complete the project by FY 2029, focusing on the Northeast market.

news.title: The Phoenix Mills’ net profit rises 11% to ₹424.05 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Phoenix Mills achieved a 10.8 percent boost in net profit after tax. The total income saw a 3.7 percent increase compared to the previous fiscal year, coupled with a remarkable 25 percent year-on-year growth in retail consumption across its operations. Improvements in operating free cash flow and liquidity further highlight Phoenix Mills' strong financial standing in Q2 FY27.

news.title: Lodha Developers’ net profit rises 28% to ₹1,013.5 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Lodha Developers reported a 28.3 percent rise in net profit after tax for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. This surge accompanied an 18.2 percent increase in total income when compared to the same quarter last year. Notably, pre-sales grew by 10 percent year-on-year, exceeding 40 percent of their annual target.

news.title: Smartworks Coworking Spaces posts ₹25.64 crore net profit in Q2 FY27
news.para: The company has reported impressive financial results for the quarter, with a total income reaching ₹605.30 crore. They saw a significant boost in revenue from operations, which jumped 39% compared to last year, coming in at ₹591 crore. Due to this growth, they have increased their revenue growth forecast for FY27 to a range of 33-35%.

news.title: Landmark Group to invest ₹1,000 crore in Gurugram commercial project
news.para: Landmark Group plans to invest around ₹1,000 crore in construction of Landmark One, its 2.1 million sq ft commercial project in Gurugram. The developer has raised ₹330 crore from SBI for the first phase and is also planning a mixed-use development on Dwarka Expressway. The two projects have combined estimated sales potential of ₹15,000 crore.

news.title: Review committee wants to wave ₹40,000 per day penalty on Nagpur smart city contractors for delays
news.para: A committee tasked with reviewing penalty-waiver applications from contractors engaged in Smart City initiatives is currently in session. These contractors have encountered delays stemming from various external hindrances impacting their work progress. The previously established penalties of Rs 40,000 per day could be rescinded based on the committee's evaluations. Recent discussions have revolved around specific land concerns and project-related packages that influence completion timelines.

news.title: Noida authority clears decks to allot 13,000 more abadi plots in urban villages
news.para: The Noida Authority has revised its Master Plan 2031 to prioritize pending allotments for farmers, with around 13,000 individuals awaiting developed plots for compensation. The amendments will specifically designate plots next to existing village abadi areas to streamline the allotment process. Following community feedback, this proposal will be forwarded to the state government for approval, potentially influencing land values in the surrounding areas as development continues.

news.title: GIS, satellite surveys help Indore civic body curb construction violations
news.para: The Indore Municipal Corporation has initiated a proactive approach using GIS technology and satellite surveillance to monitor unauthorized constructions throughout the city. In 2023 alone, they have identified 726 'Red Patches' indicating new developments. Numerous infractions have surfaced, revealing substantial deviations from sanctioned building plans. Property owners have received formal notices regarding these violations, and the corporation has already taken steps to demolish illegal structures, successfully reclaiming essential public land.
